collocations: the main bottleneck 主要瓶颈
remove the bottleneck 消除瓶颈
become a bottleneck 成为瓶颈
bottleneck.etymology: The neck of a bottle is the narrow part that limits how fast liquid pours — the metaphor is the picture. 瓶颈就是瓶子最窄的那截：流速被它卡住，画面本身就是比喻。

example.en: Profiling shows the database is the bottleneck, not the API layer.
example.zh: 性能分析显示瓶颈在数据库，不在接口层。

collocations: cache hit / miss 缓存命中/未命中
invalidate the cache 让缓存失效
warm the cache 预热缓存
cache.etymology: French cacher, 'to hide'. A cache was a hidden store of supplies; in computing, a hidden store of data. 源自法语 cacher（藏）：本指藏物资的隐蔽仓库，计算机里就是藏数据的地方。

example.en: The bug was a stale cache — the page showed prices from yesterday.
example.zh: 问题出在缓存过期上：页面显示的还是昨天的价格。

collocations: concurrency control 并发控制
concurrent requests 并发请求
handle concurrency 处理并发
concurrency.etymology: Latin con- 'together' + currere 'to run': things running together. 注意它和 parallelism 的区别：concurrency 是结构（同时应对多件事），parallelism 是真并行执行。拉丁语 con-（一起）+ currere（跑）：一起跑。

example.en: Under high concurrency, two requests updated the same row and one overwrote the other.
example.zh: 高并发下两个请求同时改了同一行，一个把另一个覆盖了。

collocations: a deadlock occurs 发生死锁
avoid deadlocks 避免死锁
deadlock detection 死锁检测
deadlock.etymology: dead + lock: a lock so complete that nothing can move — first used for traffic and negotiations, then for threads. dead（死）+ lock（锁）：锁死到一动不能动，先用于交通和谈判僵局，后用于线程。

example.en: Thread A waits for B's lock while B waits for A's — a classic deadlock.
example.zh: 线程 A 等 B 的锁，B 又等 A 的锁，经典死锁。

collocations: a failed deployment 失败的发布
deploy to production 部署到生产环境
deployment pipeline 部署流水线
deployment.etymology: de- + Latin plicare 'to fold': to deploy was to unfold troops into formation. Unfolding software onto servers kept the word. de-（解开）+ 拉丁语 plicare（折叠）：本义是把军队“展开”成阵型，后来用来指把软件展开到服务器上。

example.en: Friday deployments are banned — nobody wants a weekend incident.
example.zh: 周五禁止发布，没人想周末处理故障。

collocations: deprecated in v2 在 v2 里被弃用
deprecate an API 弃用一个接口
will be deprecated 将被弃用
deprecate.etymology: Latin de- 'away' + precari 'to pray': originally 'to pray against' something, i.e. to wish it away — then 'to disapprove', now 'please stop using this'. 拉丁语 de-（离）+ precari（祈祷）：本义是“祈祷它别发生”，后来变成“弃用”。

example.en: This endpoint is deprecated; please migrate to /v2 before the end of the quarter.
example.zh: 这个接口已经弃用了，请在本季度结束前迁到 /v2。

collocations: a fallback plan 备选方案
fall back to 退回到…
as a fallback 作为兜底
fallback.etymology: fall + back: what you fall back on when the first plan fails. 字面就是“退回去靠的东西”：主方案不行时退守的备选。

example.en: If the primary region goes down, traffic falls back to the secondary automatically.
example.zh: 主区域挂掉时，流量会自动切到备用区域。

collocations: an idempotent operation 幂等操作
make it idempotent 把它改成幂等的
idempotent retries 幂等重试
idempotent.etymology: Latin idem 'the same' + potens 'powerful', a 19th-century math term: doing it twice has the same effect as once. 数学词：拉丁语 idem（相同）+ potens（有力量），做两遍和做一遍效果相同。

example.en: Make the payment endpoint idempotent, or a retry will charge the user twice.
example.zh: 支付接口必须做成幂等的，不然一次重试就会重复扣款。

collocations: low / high latency 低/高延迟
latency budget 延迟预算
tail latency (p99) 尾延迟
reduce latency 降低延迟
latency.etymology: Latin latens, 'hidden, lying dormant'. The delay is 'hidden' time before anything visibly happens. 源自拉丁语 latens（潜伏、隐藏）：延迟就是那段“什么都没发生”的隐藏时间。

example.en: Moving the cache closer to users cut our p99 latency from 800ms to 120ms.
example.zh: 把缓存挪到离用户更近的地方后，p99 延迟从 800 毫秒降到了 120 毫秒。

collocations: a data migration 数据迁移
run the migration 执行迁移
migration script 迁移脚本
migration.etymology: Latin migrare, 'to move from one place to another' — used for birds, people, and now databases. 拉丁语 migrare（从一地迁到另一地）：鸟、人、现在轮到数据库了。

example.en: Run the migration during the maintenance window, and keep a rollback ready.
example.zh: 在维护窗口里执行迁移，并准备好回滚。

note: 单词详解二期的人工内容：词源小注（etymology，中英对照）、常用搭配（collocations）、场景例句（example，职场语境）。人工撰写和维护，先覆盖高频技术词，质量优先于数量。词源只写有把握的简明版，拿不准的宁可不写。

collocations: runtime overhead 运行时开销
adds overhead 增加开销
minimal overhead 开销极小
overhead.etymology: over + head: costs that sit 'above your head' whether you produce anything or not. over（在上）+ head（头）：悬在头顶、干不干活都要付的成本。

example.en: Encryption adds some overhead, but it is negligible at our scale.
example.zh: 加密会增加一点开销，但在我们的量级上可以忽略。

collocations: a message queue 消息队列
queue up 排队等待
process the queue 处理队列
queue.etymology: Latin cauda, 'tail', via French: a line of people looked like a tail — that is also why British 'queue' means a line of people. 源自拉丁语 cauda（尾巴），经法语而来：一排人看起来像条尾巴，英式英语里 queue 也就是“排队”。

example.en: Requests pile up in the queue whenever the workers fall behind.
example.zh: 只要处理端跟不上，请求就会在队列里堆起来。

collocations: a read replica 只读副本
replica lag 副本延迟
replication 复制（机制）
replica.etymology: Latin replicare, 'to fold back, repeat' (re- + plicare 'fold'). A replica is the original 'folded back' into a copy. 拉丁语 replicare（折回、重复，词根 plic 是“折叠”）：原件“折”出一份副本。

example.en: Reads go to the replica; writes always go to the primary.
example.zh: 读走副本，写永远走主库。

collocations: resilient to failure 对故障有韧性
build resilience 建立韧性/容错能力
a resilient design 韧性设计
resilient.etymology: Latin re- 'back' + salire 'to jump': literally 'jumping back'. A resilient system bounces back from failure. 拉丁语 re-（回）+ salire（跳）：字面是“弹回来”，所以指系统出故障后能自己恢复。

example.en: The service stayed resilient during the outage — it retried, degraded gracefully, and never lost data.
example.zh: 故障期间这个服务很抗造：重试、优雅降级，数据一条没丢。

collocations: retry the request 重试请求
retry with backoff 带退避地重试
automatic retries 自动重试
retry.etymology: re- 'again' + try. 'Try' itself comes from Old French trier, 'to sift, select' — you sift once more. re-（再次）+ try（尝试）；try 本身源自古法语 trier（筛选），再筛一遍。

example.en: Retry with exponential backoff, but cap it at three attempts.
example.zh: 用指数退避重试，但最多试三次。

collocations: a robust solution 稳健的方案
robust error handling 健壮的错误处理
robust enough for production 足够健壮、能上生产
robust.etymology: Latin robustus, from robur, 'oak tree'. Hard oak wood became the image of strength. 源自拉丁语 robur（橡树），橡木坚硬，所以引申为强壮、可靠。

example.en: The parser needs to be robust against malformed input from third-party feeds.
example.zh: 这个解析器必须扛得住第三方数据源的畸形输入。

collocations: roll back the deployment 回滚这次发布
a rollback plan 回滚方案
rollback to the previous version 回滚到上一版
rollback.etymology: roll + back: roll the system back like a log to where it was. roll（滚动）+ back（回）：像滚木头一样把系统滚回之前的状态。

example.en: Error rate spiked after the release, so we rolled back within five minutes.
example.zh: 发布后错误率飙升，我们五分钟内就回滚了。

collocations: highly scalable 高度可扩展的
scale horizontally / vertically 水平/垂直扩展
scalable architecture 可扩展架构
scalable.etymology: From Latin scala, 'ladder' — that is why old dictionaries list 'climbable' first. The computing sense comes from 'scale' as size: a system that can climb to a bigger size. 源自拉丁语 scala（梯子），所以老词典把“可攀登的”排第一；计算机义取 scale 的“规模”义：能爬到更大规模。

example.en: We need the design to be scalable before the marketing launch doubles our traffic.
example.zh: 市场推广会让流量翻倍，设计必须先做到可扩展。

collocations: shard by user id 按用户 id 分片
a shard key 分片键
sharding strategy 分片策略
shard.etymology: Old English sceard, 'a fragment, a broken piece' (of pottery). Sharding breaks one big database into pieces. 古英语 sceard（碎片、破陶片）：分片就是把一个大库打成碎片分开放。

example.en: We shard by tenant id so one noisy tenant cannot slow down the others.
example.zh: 我们按租户 id 分片，这样一个闹腾的租户拖不慢其他人。

collocations: take a snapshot 做一个快照
a snapshot of the database 数据库快照
snapshot testing 快照测试
snapshot.etymology: snap + shot: a quick hunter's shot, then a quick photo — a frozen picture of one moment. snap（快速）+ shot（一击）：本是猎人的速射，后指快照：某一瞬间的定格。

example.en: Take a snapshot of the volume before running the migration.
example.zh: 跑迁移之前，先给这个卷做个快照。

collocations: a stateless service 无状态服务
stateless by design 设计上无状态
keep it stateless 保持无状态
stateless.etymology: state from Latin status, 'standing, condition', plus -less 'without'. 无状态 = 不记着上一次请求发生过什么。state 源自拉丁语 status（状态），加 -less（无）。

example.en: If the service is stateless, we can add instances behind the load balancer freely.
example.zh: 只要服务是无状态的，我们就能在负载均衡后面随意加实例。

collocations: throttle requests 限制请求速率
get throttled 被限流
throttling policy 限流策略
throttle.etymology: From 'throat': to throttle was to choke. Choking the flow of a pipe became limiting any flow. 来自 throat（喉咙），本义是掐脖子；掐住管道的流量，就成了“限流”。

example.en: The API throttles us at 100 requests per minute, so we added a queue.
example.zh: 接口把我们限在每分钟 100 次请求，所以我们加了个队列。

collocations: high throughput 高吞吐
throughput of 10k requests per second 每秒一万请求的吞吐量
max out throughput 打满吞吐
throughput.etymology: A plain compound: through + put — how much a factory could put through in a day, later borrowed by computing. 直白的复合词：through（穿过）+ put（放），原指工厂一天能“过”多少货，后来被计算机借用。

example.en: Batching the writes tripled throughput without adding any servers.
example.zh: 把写入改成批量后，没加一台服务器，吞吐量涨到了三倍。

collocations: a 30-second timeout 30 秒超时
time out 超时（动词）
set a timeout 设置超时
timeout.etymology: time + out: the time runs out. Originally a sports pause; in computing, a deadline that cancels the wait. time（时间）+ out（用完）：时间耗尽。原指体育暂停，后指等待的截止线。

example.en: The request timed out because the downstream service never responded.
example.zh: 下游服务一直没响应，这个请求就超时了。
